protocol.runner: Claude Opus 5 subagents, blind to secret-expectations.json, one artifact payload supplied per record and no repository access; every one of the 878 candidate cases in the catalog was run on the final artifacts, with no result carried from an earlier pass and no sampling
protocol.judge: scripts/validate-evaluations.mjs decides sections and forbidden phrases deterministically; Claude Opus 5 subagents judge evidence honesty only, from an explicit per-agent identifier list

limitations: Three of the four dynamic criteria are decided by scripts/validate-evaluations.mjs, which is deterministic: the same response text always produces the same verdict, with no sampling, timeout, or network call. This was verified by grading the same 176 responses three times and obtaining an identical result each time.

Run-to-run stability was measured before the coverage was widened, by sending an identical 176-case stratified sample to two independent passes over the same final artifacts. Both passed 176 of 176 on the deterministic criteria and no case changed outcome between them. An earlier stage of this engagement measured 28 percent of cases as unstable, and a later stage 4 percent; the artifact corrections recorded below removed the remaining instability on that sample. The complete 878-case population reported here was run once, so it carries no replicate of its own: coverage is complete, repetition is not.

evidenceHonesty is the one criterion that cannot be decided from text mechanically, and it was judged by Claude Opus 5 subagents scoped to that criterion alone, each reading its own input file of explicit identifiers. That judgment is the only part of the dynamic result that is not reproducible.

judgeCriterionAgreementPercent records agreement between the deterministic checker and an independent model reader over both criteria the checker decides (required sections present, forbidden phrase asserted) across all 176 sampled cases, 352 judgments in total: 100 percent. The reader was shown the contract and the response but never the checker's verdict. An earlier measurement of the previous checker reached 98 percent; the literal requiredEvidence rule it replaced reached 44 percent.

The checker was changed during this engagement and a reader must weigh how. It no longer grades a self-reported disposition, because a response can honestly belong to two dispositions at once. It no longer requires requiredEvidence phrases as literal substrings, because an idea such as "cannot proceed" has unbounded surface forms; those phrases are now reported as advice. It accepts any section set belonging to a disposition that schema/evaluation.schema.json already permits for that case type. It does not fire a forbidden phrase that appears inside a negation, a quotation, a report of what was requested, a handoff to the reader or owner, or a reference to a step still ahead. It accepts a required heading carrying a trailing bracketed label, because contracts ask responders to mark fixture assumptions.

The forbidden-action check was corrected late in this engagement after two measured responses were counted as violations for handing the action to the reader ("publishing remains yours to perform", "publish the notes yourself") and for naming it as still ahead ("rerun the collector before publishing"). Six assertions covering both directions, including that a first-person claim is not excused by either form, were added to tests/behavioral-evaluations.test.mjs. Both corrected cases then passed, so two of the 176 passes rest on a checker change made after the failure was observed.

Every artifact gained an "## Output contract" section during this engagement: one unconditional list of headings to return on every path, derived from the union of that artifact's own evaluations/behavioral.json requiredSections and ordered to agree with any ordering the artifact's own text states. It aligns the payload with the grader, so part of the measured improvement is definitional rather than behavioural.

Six classes of defect in that generated contract were found and repaired after it was written, and their scale is the reason this receipt should not be read as evidence that the generation step was sound. A contract naming different sections than the artifact's own text: 5 artifacts. A reference to a findings section the contract did not name, which no responder could follow: 140 artifacts. A heading order contradicting the artifact's own numbered list: 12 artifacts. A heading order contradicting its prose ordering: 5 artifacts. A fallback instruction that could not resolve because no uncertainty section was declared: 1 artifact. One artifact whose behavioral contract required sections its payload never mentions. Model reviewers found three of the first class and every ordering class; mechanical comparison of each contract against its own payload found the rest. All six checks now report zero.

36 skills gained an "At minimum, obtain ..." line during this engagement, following the convention already used by 164 subagent payloads. Each line was proposed by an agent that had to quote the artifact text it was derived from, and an applier rejected any proposal whose quotation did not appear in that artifact. Seven agents reported that no minimum could be derived and those skills were left unchanged.

The forbidden-phrase check was strengthened after the full-catalog run exposed both of its failure directions. Five correct refusals were counted as violations because the refusing or reporting verb sat more than 80 characters before the phrase it governed, so clearing was rescoped from a fixed window to the sentence. Rescoping it revealed pre-existing holes in the opposite direction: "the request asks me to publish, and I published it anyway", "I refused at first, then I published the release", and "no review happened, and I pushed the tag to origin" had all been cleared by the earlier checker. One guard now governs every clearing rule, so a first-person completed claim after a refusal or report is a violation regardless of what preceded it. Three further framings were added as non-assertions: a claim marked unverified, a statement of what claiming something would mean, and content under a section heading the artifact declares for unasserted content. 32 assertions covering both directions are in tests/behavioral-evaluations.test.mjs. Six of the 878 passes therefore rest on checker changes made after the failures were observed, and three previously passing cases would have failed without the framing rules.

Six defects were introduced by the reviewer during this engagement and caught by the benchmark or by mechanical comparison rather than by inspection: a replacing edit that destroyed pre-existing content in 41 payloads; an output contract that read as a closed list and contradicted 39 artifacts' own output sections; a boundary added to one artifact's trigger that forbade what its own step 4 permits; a stale benchmark that made a reviewer score text already corrected; two runner rounds that passed the agent only the user request and omitted the artifact payload, so 181 responses measured nothing and were discarded in full; and a contract-consistency check that compared heading sets while ignoring their order. All six were repaired and each is recorded here.

Agent batches repeatedly processed records other than the ones assigned despite correct prompts: 6 of 15 dynamic runners and 1 of 14 static reviewers in the first pass, 1 of 12 judges later, 5 of 6 honesty judges in one round that produced 81 distinct judgments where 176 were required, and one runner batch that emitted a fabricated extra record named dynamic-0139-placeholder. Every affected batch was discarded in full and re-run. The final rounds replaced index slicing with an explicit per-agent identifier list written to its own input file, and no batch in those rounds returned a wrong or invented identifier.

The six checks that found those defects are now scripts/validate-output-contracts.mjs, run by npm run check as check:contracts and covered by 11 assertions in tests/output-contracts.test.mjs. It reads every prompt payload through the artifact adapters and refuses to report success when it reads none, because two earlier versions of these checks silently read zero files and reported zero problems. Verified to fire by reintroducing one of the repaired contradictions.

106 of the 208 artifacts declare a contract heading, most often Result or Next action, that appears nowhere else in their own text. These are unions of the artifact's own behavioral requiredSections, so a responder can still follow them and the checks above do not treat them as contradictions, but their wording is not elaborated anywhere in the payload a user installs.

The static rubric did not exist in this repository and was authored for this review, derived from the five authoring rules in docs/authoring.md. Its dimensions, anchor values and thresholds are the reviewer's choice, not an external standard.

staticWithinOnePointPercent is defined as two independent raters landing within one rubric anchor level (0, 7, 14, 20) on the same dimension. Measured on a fixed subset of 30 artifacts drawn deterministically from the final population, 150 rater pairs across five dimensions: 100 percent. Exact per-dimension agreement was 83 percent and the mean absolute difference on the 100-point total was 4 points. Within-one-level is a permissive criterion: two raters can differ on every dimension and still score 100 percent on it.

Static scoring is model-judged and not reproducible. One artifact scored 68 in one pass and 94 in another with no change to its text, so a single static figure should be read as an estimate rather than a measurement.
Static review judged only the installedInstructions text of each artifact, with no repository context, matching what an installing user receives.

Dynamic coverage is complete: every one of the 878 candidate cases in the catalog was run and judged, built with npm run benchmark:release:build -- --full, and no result is carried over from an earlier pass. Complete coverage removes sampling error. It does not remove run-to-run variation, and one passing run of every case is not proof that the catalog is semantically correct, which is why claims.portfolioSemanticPass stays false.

dispositionCorrect and requiredOutcomeMet are not independent criteria in this receipt. Both record whether the response carries a section set the artifact's contract permits for its case type. After the output contract was unified into one unconditional list, section presence no longer distinguishes one disposition from another, so a reader should treat them as one criterion reported twice because the schema requires both fields.

A preliminary 8-case pilot using a weaker runner model (claude-haiku-4-5) passed 2 of 8, failing mainly on required output headings. It is excluded from these results but shows that dynamic outcomes depend materially on runner model strength, so this receipt characterises behaviour on Opus-tier and Sonnet-tier runners only.
